MFA No.6465/2018 is filed by the KSRTC and MFA No.4563/2022 is filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 20.4.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in MVC No.4319/2017.
2.

Facts giving rise to filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 29.6.2017 at about 2.35 p.m.,
when the deceased Nagaraj was crossing the road on Old Madras Road, Opp.

To Sri Rama Hospital,
at that time, a KSRTC bus bearing Registration No.KA-40-F-936, which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the deceased.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
On service of summons, the respondent appeared through counsel and filed written statement in which the averments made in the petition were denied.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove their case, examined claimant No.2 as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
On behalf of respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1, but no document was produced.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia
, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.13,30,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the KSRTC to deposit the said compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeals are filed.
Mr.F.S.Dabali, learned counsel for the KSRTC has raised the following contentions:
Re: Negligence The accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased himself.
The deceased was crossing the main road negligently and without following the traffic rules.
The Tribunal is not justified in holding that the driver of the bus alone was negligent in causing the accident.
The driver of the bus, who has been examined as DW-1 has specifically deposed that the deceased was a pedestrian and he was negligently crossing the main road.
Even though the driver of the bus tried his best efforts to avoid the accident, he could not control the vehicle.
He further contended that even as per complaint Ex.P-2, spot mahazar Ex.P-3, sketch Ex.P-4, it is very clear that the deceased was crossing the main road.
Therefore, it is clear that the deceased was negligent in causing the accident.
But the Tribunal has not considered this aspect of the NC: 2023:KHC:33135 matter and has erred in holding that the driver of the bus alone was negligent in causing the accident.

Re: Quantum of compensation:

Firstly, the claimants claim that the deceased was earning an income of Rs.15,000/-
per month.
But they have not produced any document to show that he was earning the said income.

In the absence of proof of income, the income of Rs.9,000/- p.m.
assessed by the Tribunal, is on the higher side.
Secondly, the claimant Nos.2 and 5 are major son and daughter.
They are married and living separately and they are not depending on the income of the deceased.
The Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses.
Thirdly, since the claimants have not established the income, they are not entitled for future prospects.

Fourthly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased,
the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Fifthly, the KSRTC has already paid an interim compensation of Rs.15,000/- to the claimants.
Hence, the said amount needs to be deducted from the total compensation.

Lastly, in view of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS - V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018 AND CONNECTED MATTERS DISPOSED OF ON 24.8.2020), the rate of interest granted by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount is on the higher side.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following counter-contentions:
NC: 2023:KHC:33135 Re: Negligence The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.
PW-1 in his evidence has categorically stated that due to the negligence of the driver of the bus, the accident has occurred.
Even as per sketch, the deceased was at the edge of the road and the driver of the bus has come to the extreme right side of the road and dashed to the deceased.
The driver of the bus has been examined as RW-1 and in his evidence except deposing that the deceased was a pedestrian, nothing worthwhile has been elicited.
He further contended that immediately after the accident, FIR has been registered against the driver of the bus and after investigation, charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the bus.
The driver of the bus was driving the bus at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.

Re: Quantum of compensation Firstly, the claimants claim that the deceased was working as a mason and earning Rs.15,000/-
per month.
But the Tribunal is not justified in taking the monthly notional income of the deceased as merely as Rs.9,000/-.
Secondly, PW-1 in his evidence has stated that the claimants are entirely depending on the income of the deceased.
The Tribunal instead of deducting 1/4th of the income has wrongly deducted 1/3rd of the income.

Thirdly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 25% of the established income towards 'future prospects' should be the warrant - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:33135 where the deceased was between the age of 45-60 years.

sentences.text: Under the Motor Vehicles Act in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal, the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in the civil case.

No doubt, before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:33135 to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.
After all it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

In the case of MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as hereinbelow:
"25.

entities.text: MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Dulcina Fernandes, this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

This Court,
however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie, materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:33135 beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
After the accident, the police have drawn spot mahazar and sketch as per Exs.P-3 and 4.

By going through the evidence of the parties and materials available on record, it is very clear that the deceased was crossing the road and the driver of the bus has come to the extreme right side of the road and dashed to the deceased.

Even though the driver of the bus has deposed that the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased, but no complaint has been lodged in the police station and even he has not informed his superior authority
. Considering all these aspects of the matter, the Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the bus alone was negligent in causing the accident.
Hence, there is no error in the said finding of the Tribunal.
RE: QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION 10.
The claimants claim that the deceased was working as a mason and earning Rs.15,000/- per month - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:33135
They have not produced any documents to prove the same.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Smt. Shanthamma vs The Managing Director Ksrtc on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32996633/

sentences.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2017, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.11,000/- p.m.

To the aforesaid income, 25% has been rightly added by the Tribunal on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'PRANAY SETHI' (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.13,750/-.
The claimant Nos.2 and 5 are majors and married.
Considering the same, the Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and taken remaining amount as his contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 45 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '14'.
Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:33135 Rs.15,40,000/- (Rs.13,750*12*14*2/3) on account of 'loss of dependency'.

In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate'
and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.
Claimant No.1, wife of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of spousal consortium'.

In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE'
(supra), claimant Nos.2, 3 and 5, children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium' and claimant No.4, mother of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) Both the appeals are disposed of.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.17,55,000/- as against Rs.13,30,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

In view of judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE'
(supra), the compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.

e) The KSRTC is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
f) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
g) The amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
h) In view of the order dated 13.9.2023 passed by this Court, the claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 701 days in filing the appeal.
